work_order.understanding: Reproduced against src/web/pages.js: for all five routes in all five states (25 combinations), document.querySelectorAll('h1').length is 0 and the first heading inside <main id="main"> is always an <h2>. The cause is in the shared layout, not in any one page: layout() (src/web/pages.js:40) emits the skip link, header, <main> and footer but never a page-level heading, and panel() (src/web/pages.js:81) hard-codes <h2> for every panel title. panel() is already correct — once a document has an <h1>, its <h2> panel titles sit exactly one level beneath it, which is the hierarchy the issue asks for. The whole fix is therefore one element in layout(), plus the type rule to render it. Five pages, twenty-five shells, one line of markup, no per-page work.
work_order.root_cause: layout() in src/web/pages.js:40 renders <main id="main"> with ${content} as its only child and no page-level heading, so every document's heading hierarchy begins at the <h2> that panel() emits.
work_order.approach: Render exactly one <h1> as the first child of <main id="main"> in layout(), using the same `title` value the document title already interpolates, so the h1 text and the <title> can never drift apart and no new copy table is introduced. Style it with the existing display size already in the stylesheet rather than adding a fourth type size, and zero its margin because #main is a CSS grid whose gap already spaces children. Deliberately do NOT change panel(): its <h2> becomes correct automatically once the h1 exists, and demoting it further would break the existing error-panel test from #38. Deliberately do NOT touch .sdlc/memory/** (see risks).

triage.diagnosis: The plan cannot be built as described. Its files[2] edits .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, and on a ticket branch the effective rule set reserves the whole of .sdlc/memory/ — not because config.yml lists it, but because reservedRules() appends '.sdlc/memory/**' whenever the head branch is neither sdlc/project-* nor memory/* (src is .sdlc/bin/lib/guards.js:127). The implement stage's prepare job fetched the approved work order and refused it before any code was written, so nothing of the implementation exists and nothing is worth resuming. The planner made a wrong assumption and said so in its own risks[4]: it claimed the file 'is not in forbidden_paths, so the diff gate will allow it'. That reasoning read only the config list; the framework's own reserved rules are unioned on top of it (guards.js:127 RESERVED + cfg.forbidden_paths + branch-dependent rules), so a path can be reserved without appearing in config.yml at all. The plan is otherwise sound and even prescribes the repair: risks[4] states the selectors.md edit 'records a hook, it does not affect behaviour' and is 'safe to drop'. Replan with files[2] removed and the other two edits (src/web/pages.js, src/web/styles.css) and the test file unchanged. Not transient, not a code defect, not a framework bug in the guard — the guard is right and refused exactly what it should. Separately, no stage between the plan and the implementer ever ran that check, which is why a whole council was spent to learn this; that gap is recorded below.
